title: Pulmonary Tuberculosis: Recognition, Isolation and Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults and children with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) in primary care, the emergency department (ED) or hospital in Saudi Arabia: who to test, specimens and the Xpert MTB/RIF test (detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) and rifampicin (RIF) resistance), interpretation, airborne isolation and staff protection, notification, contact management and referral to the TB service or drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) centre. Uses the Saudi MOH National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) manual 2021 and a UK hospital TB policy based on NICE NG33. Drug treatment is started and supervised by the TB service and is not dosed here.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-22.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Only pages 4 to 34 of the Saudi NTP manual could be read; the treatment, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) testing, notification and contact sections were not opened, so no drug doses are given.
The World Health Organization 2019 TB infection-control guideline could not be opened; hospital isolation rules come from a UK trust policy based on NICE NG33.
UK notification rules in the trust policy do not apply in Saudi Arabia; Saudi notification is to the province or district TB coordinator.
Typical normal values are not given in these sources.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: Pulmonary and laryngeal TB spread by airborne droplets when patients cough (DBTH TB policy 2023, Section 6). Most patients are no longer infectious after 2 weeks of appropriate treatment if they respond and have no drug-resistance risk (DBTH TB policy 2023, Section 6.1). Rifampicin resistance detected on Xpert signals possible multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB), which needs a different regimen and DR-TB centre care (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Algorithm 1 Step 3, p. 24). People living with HIV have higher TB risk and should be screened at every visit (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Section 2, p. 8).

symptoms: Night sweats and fever (DBTH TB policy 2023, Section 7 and Appendix 2).
physicalSigns: Swollen neck glands (DBTH TB policy 2023, Appendix 2).
Chest X-ray abnormalities suggesting TB (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Algorithm 1 footnote 1, p. 22).
redFlags: Rifampicin resistance detected: MDR-TB risk assessment and referral to a DR-TB treatment site (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Algorithm 1 Step 3, p. 24).
HIV with CD4 count 100 cells/µL or less or severe illness: use the HIV algorithm (Algorithm 4) (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Algorithm 1 footnote 1, p. 22).
Suspected MDR-TB in hospital: negative-pressure room with at least 15 air changes per hour (DBTH TB policy 2023, Table 1).
Laryngeal TB or extensive cavitation: keep isolated beyond 2 weeks (DBTH TB policy 2023, Section 6.1).
precipitants: HIV infection (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Section 2, p. 8).
Household or close contact with a TB patient (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Section 2, p. 8).
Previous TB treatment or other MDR-TB risk factors (DBTH TB policy 2023, Section 4; Saudi NTP manual 2021, Algorithm 1 Step 3, p. 24).

clinicalManagement.title: Suspect TB and protect others
actions: Give the patient a surgical mask and see them in a single room with the door closed, away from immunocompromised patients (DBTH TB policy 2023, Section 6 and 6.1).
Staff wear an FFP3 respirator, fit-tested, for contact over 5 minutes or cough-inducing procedures (DBTH TB policy 2023, Table 2 and Section 6.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Collect specimens and test
actions: Collect two specimens: test the first by Xpert MTB/RIF and smear, keep the second for culture and drug susceptibility testing (Saudi NTP manual 2021, p. 19 and Algorithm 1 footnote 3, p. 22).
Primary health care centres identify and refer suspected cases for diagnosis (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Section 2, p. 14).

clinicalManagement.title: Act on the result
actions: MTB detected, rifampicin resistance not detected: start first-line TB treatment through the TB service (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Algorithm 1 Step 2, p. 23).

Rifampicin resistance detected: assess MDR-TB risk; high risk starts a rifampicin-resistant (RR) or MDR regimen at a DR-TB site; low risk repeat Xpert on a second sample (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Algorithm 1 Step 3, p. 24).
MTB not detected: re-evaluate and test further (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Algorithm 1 Step 5, p. 24).

clinicalManagement.title: Hospital isolation
actions: Keep the door shut and patient masked outside the room until at least 2 weeks of treatment (DBTH TB policy 2023, Section 6.1).
Suspected or confirmed MDR-TB: negative-pressure room and FFP3 for all contact (DBTH TB policy 2023, Tables 1 and 2).
Limit visitors to close contacts; discourage children (DBTH TB policy 2023, Section 6.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Notify and manage contacts
actions: Notify the province or district TB coordinator; private facilities must notify all TB patients (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Section 2, p. 16).
Screen household and close contacts and give preventive therapy as per MOH policy (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Section 2, p. 8).

clinicalManagement.title: Discharge with supervised treatment
actions: Arrange directly observed therapy and inform the TB nurse before discharge (DBTH TB policy 2023, Section 8).
Drugs can be supplied at home or in facilities to suit the patient (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Section 2, p. 8).

medicationPlan.note: TB treatment is started and supervised by the national TB programme after diagnosis; first-line regimen for drug-susceptible TB and RR/MDR regimens at DR-TB sites (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Algorithm 1 Steps 2 and 3, pp. 23 to 24). Doses are not listed because the treatment section of the manual could not be opened. diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Adults and children with signs, symptoms or chest X-ray changes suggesting TB (Saudi NTP manual 2021, Algorithm 1 footnote 1, p. 22).
Xpert MTB/RIF on the first of two specimens; smear microscopy is for treatment follow-up, not diagnosis (Saudi NTP manual 2021, pp. 15 and 19).

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: End of hospital isolation, drug-susceptible TB
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: At least 2 weeks of appropriate treatment, adherence, resolved cough, clinical improvement such as afebrile for a week, no extensive cavitation or laryngeal TB, no MDR-TB risk or rifampicin resistance excluded (DBTH TB policy 2023, Section 6.1).
Smear negative on 3 sputum samples a week apart, ideally culture negative (DBTH TB policy 2023, Table 1).

teaching.scope: Adults and children with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) in primary care, the emergency department (ED) or hospital in Saudi Arabia: who to test, specimens and the Xpert MTB/RIF test (detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) and rifampicin (RIF) resistance), interpretation, airborne isolation and staff protection, notification, contact management and referral to the TB service or drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) centre. Uses the Saudi MOH National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) manual 2021 and a UK hospital TB policy based on NICE NG33. Drug treatment is started and supervised by the TB service and is not dosed here.
learningObjectives: Use Xpert MTB/RIF as the first test and act on the result.
Notify, manage contacts and refer to the TB service or DR-TB centre.
pitfalls: Ending isolation in laryngeal or cavitary TB at 2 weeks.
keyPoints: Smear is for follow-up, not diagnosis.
Isolation usually ends after 2 weeks of treatment with clinical response and no resistance risk.

patientEducation: TB is curable with a full course of tablets taken every day.
Wear a mask and cover your cough until your doctor says you are no longer infectious.
Family and close contacts need screening.
lifestyleAndDiet: Good ventilation at home; avoid crowded indoor places while infectious.
mdtReferrals: Primary care; respiratory or infectious diseases physician; TB coordinator and TB nurse; infection prevention and control; public health for contacts; DR-TB centre for resistant TB.
dischargeCriteria: Diagnosis confirmed and treatment started, isolation criteria met or home isolation advice given, directly observed therapy arranged, notification done, contacts listed (DBTH TB policy 2023, Section 8; Saudi NTP manual 2021, Section 2).
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: TB service follow-up with sputum at 2, 4 and 6 months of treatment (Saudi NTP manual 2021, p. 14); contact screening and preventive therapy (Saudi NTP manual 2021, p. 8).
